chapter: Small group, new sound and Europe
title: Backing Sinatra and Tony Bennett
summary: They discuss recordings and appearances with Sinatra, Bennett and Ella, and the Sands in Las Vegas.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Well, I mean, then -- I mean isn't that when that new thing that -- Basie made some record sessions back of Sinatra, or back of Tony Bennett? When did that begin? You know, when it started -- when the band was starting to back up --
Well that isn't -- but, that did become, sort of, kind of important -- but, it really wasn't good. I don't think it was -- well --
-- it may have been good financially, but it wasn't very good for the band's image, was it?
You know, it became -- it began to look as though it were an accompanying travelling band.
But, that lasted a long time.
But, it lasted -- yeah -- it lasted awhile. We did quite a bit of that.
Did you go abroad with singers like that?
Did you go abroad with Tony Benett? You did, didn't you?
Yeah. We went abroad with Tony Benett, we went abroad with -- when we did that thing with Frank Sinatra.
And then we did -- that gave us came again with him at the Palladium.
Yes. And you were over there with Ella.
Well, I mean, in a way, really -- what happened was that competition and changing times -- it was so hard to keep going.
I mean, they were looking for gimmicks, in a sense, to keep -- for the public to keep buying the product.
But, also, the singers had gotten a little too important.
And, we did the Las Vegas thing, you know -- this thing in Vegas, and what-not.
We did the recording first, didn't we? We did the recording with him first, and then we went into --
And, then we recorded on stage there.
And then after that, the public wanted to see the two together, you know.
That's it. Actually it profitted -- it did him good the same way -- it was good for Sinatra.
Well, I mean, that was really a matter of -- well, you know --
-- that was a plain matter of economics -- a matter of keeping the band together.
